title: Extract GST from an inclusive amount
note: Assumes the whole amount is taxable at 10%. The function returns an unrounded binary floating-point result. Use ROUND(...,2) where cent rounding is required; the reviewer decides the treatment.

title: Add GST to an exclusive amount
note: Assumes a wholly taxable amount and the default 10% rate. This does not classify a supply or establish a credit entitlement.

title: Label an Australian financial year
note: The default start month is July. Supply StartMonth for another year end; the function labels a date and does not determine a reporting obligation.

title: Build a straight-line modelling schedule
expected: 200.00 in each of five columns; total 1,000.00.
note: Cost and life are supplied assumptions. This is a modelling schedule, not an ATO Division 40 tax calculation.

title: Build a diminishing-balance modelling schedule
note: Uses 200% of the straight-line rate and writes off the remaining balance in the final year. It does not establish a tax deduction.

title: Inspect the first month of a loan schedule
expected: Debt issued 100,000.00; opening 100,000.00; interest 416.67; payment -1,887.12; closing 98,529.54; principal repaid 1,470.46. Each figure is displayed to two decimals.
note: A 100,000 loan at 5% over 60 monthly payments. TAKE selects the first column of the six-row schedule. Remove TAKE to spill the full schedule; confirm the loan terms and timing separately.

title: Discount three unpaid lease payments
note: The 5% rate is per payment period and the payments are in arrears. The reviewer establishes the lease term, included payments and applicable discount rate.

title: Convert an effective annual rate
note: The input is a 5% effective annual rate. This conversion is not the same as dividing a nominal annual rate by 12.

title: Calculate rates for dated periods
note: The default is Actual/365. Supply the required convention and check how the final period is inferred; the function does not choose a contractual day count basis.

title: Calculate an annual return from dated cash flows
note: One outflow of 1,000 followed by an inflow of 1,100 one year later. Other cash flow patterns may have multiple or no solutions; inspect the inputs and validate the result.
